name: Codex CLI
invoke: spawn the `waypost-<role>` agent, or `codex exec "$(waypost agents show <role>) <target>"`
notes: Codex has project-level agents now: .codex/agents/<name>.toml with name, description and developer_instructions (the system prompt), plus optional model, model_reasoning_effort and sandbox_mode. `sandbox_mode = "read-only"` is emitted, which is the one place a harness enforces the roles' read-only contract rather than asking for it. The older ~/.codex/prompts custom prompts are deprecated by OpenAI in favour of skills, so waypost no longer writes them; project agents need no follow-up copy step, so this entry has no after_install. `model_reasoning_effort` uses `{effort}` through `roles.effort.map`, which only covers Codex's own documented values (low/medium/high) — deliberately not inventing an `xhigh` or similar tier no vendor doc names. Every shipped role is effort:max today, which this maps to "high"; revisit the map if Codex's own scale changes. The official docs page could not be fetched directly (learn.chatgpt.com returned 404 to the fetcher); the format is taken from a reference that cites it — check once against `codex --help`.
